name: Republic of Indonesia
alt: Republic of the United States of Indonesia

predecessors.name: Dutch East Indies
predecessors.text: Java, Madura and Sumatra, the land of which the Netherlands later recognised the Republic as the de facto authority (Linggadjati, November 1946); the whole of the Dutch East Indies after 27 December…

ledger.x: 1945: Sukarno and Hatta proclaim Indonesian independence (17 August), two days after Japan's surrender.
October 1945: British forces, with Dutch NICA troops, land in the Republic's cities.

1946: the Yogyakarta page says the city 'became the capital of the Indonesian Republic from 1946 to 1948'; the Revolution page says the Dutch landed at Jakarta with British help and 'could not hold the city', so 'The Republican leadership thus established themselves in the city of Yogyakarta'.

1946: the Netherlands recognises the Republic's de facto authority over Java, Madura and Sumatra in the Linggadjati Agreement, 'concluded in November 1946' (the Dutch Lower House ratified a stripped-down version on 25 March 1947, which the Republic rejected).

November 1946: the Linggadjati Agreement, 'brokered by the British and concluded in November 1946', recognises the Republic as the de facto authority over Java, Madura and Sumatra and ends the first phase.
1947: Operation Product begins.
1947: Operation Product takes the plantation and port regions, held at the ceasefire of 4 August.
1947: the ceasefire of 4 August 1947 under UN Security Council Resolution 27 ends the offensive; the Renville Agreement of January 1948 froze the Van Mook line.

1948: Operation Kraai (19 December) takes Yogyakarta, 'By the following day it had conquered the city of Yogyakarta'; the president and vice-president are captured and exiled to Bangka; the Emergency Government 'was established in West Sumatra'.
1948: Operation Kraai begins (19 December); the Dutch conquer Yogyakarta by the next day.
19 December 1948: with Yogyakarta invaded in Operation Kraai the capital 'was moved to Bukittinggi', where the Emergency Government was set up in West Sumatra.

Roem-Van Roijen page: the agreement 'was an agreement made between Indonesian republicans and the Netherlands on 7 May 1949' (Indonesian forces to 'cease all guerrilla activities', Republican government restored in Yogyakarta) and 'the final Dutch forces left the Yogyakarta region on 30 June'; the Yogyakarta page says…
6 July 1949: 'republican leaders Sukarno and Hatta returned to the capital', i.e.
1949: Darul Islam rises in West Java.
1949: the Republic becomes the Republic of the United States of Indonesia.
1949: the Netherlands transfers sovereignty (27 December) over all of the Dutch East Indies except Dutch New Guinea, ending the Revolution.
1949: the fighting ends with the transfer of sovereignty.
1950: the federation becomes a unitary republic (17 August).
1951: Kahar Muzakkar's rebels in South Sulawesi join Darul Islam ('joined the Darul Islam movement in 1951'); the page gives no month.
1953: Aceh rises.

15 February 1958: 'The PRRI was proclaimed to have been established on 15 February 1958 by Lieutenant Colonel Ahmad Hussein'; the Permesta rebels, founded on 2 March 1957, 'had pledged allegiance with the PRRI on 17 February 1958'.
ledger.cpn: Revolutionary Government of the Republic of Indonesia

ledger.x: 28 September 1961: the infobox lists the PRRI government's disestablishment; the Permesta page says its last remnants 'surrendered and were given amnesty in 1961' (Kawilarang surrendered on 14 April 1961, Sumual on 20 October 1961, and the last commander, Kumontoy, in early 1962).
ledger.cpn: Revolutionary Government of the Republic of Indonesia

ledger.x: 1962: peace in Aceh.

1962: Indonesian paratroopers land near Merauke (24 June) after Sukarno's order of 19 December 1961 to prepare an invasion; 'The Dutch retained control over their colony on the western half of New Guinea' since 1949.
1962: the New York Agreement (15 August) ends the fighting; the Dutch are to hand West New Guinea to the UN on 1 October 1962.
1962: Darul Islam ends in West Java.
1963: UNTEA hands West New Guinea to Indonesia (1 May).
1965: the last Darul Islam rising ends.
1975: Indonesia invades East Timor (7 December), nine days after Fretilin declared independence on 28 November; Batugade fell on 8 October and Balibo on about 16 October.
1976: the contest ends in annexation (17 July); resistance continues, and the UN keeps Portugal as administering power.
1976: Indonesia annexes East Timor (17 July): 'Indonesia formally annexed East Timor as its 27th province'.
1999: Indonesia leaves East Timor.

wars.name: Indonesian National Revolution
wars.outcome: The Netherlands transferred sovereignty on 27 December 1949 over the whole Dutch East Indies except western New Guinea after two offensives (Operation Product, July 1947; Operation Kraai, December 1948) and the Renville Agreement (January 1948).

wars.name: Darul Islam rebellion
wars.outcome: The rebellion ended region by region: South Kalimantan in 1959, Aceh by negotiated peace (1959-1962), West Java in June-August 1962, South Sulawesi in February 1965.

wars.name: PRRI and Permesta rebellion
wars.outcome: The PRRI government was disestablished on 28 September 1961 (infobox) and the last Permesta remnants surrendered and were given amnesty in 1961, the last commander in early 1962.

wars.name: West New Guinea dispute
wars.outcome: Operation Trikora (ordered 19 December 1961) and the 1962 infiltrations led to the New York Agreement (15 August 1962), UNTEA (planned from 1 October 1962) and the transfer to Indonesia on 1 May 1963.

wars.name: Indonesian occupation of East Timor
wars.outcome: Indonesia invaded (7 December 1975), annexed East Timor (17 July 1976) and withdrew after the 30 August 1999 referendum; independence 20 May 2002.

wars.name: Free Aceh Movement insurgency
wars.outcome: Hasan di Tiro founded GAM and declared independence in 1976; the insurgency revived in 1989, prompting a decade-long military campaign; the Yudhoyono administration 'reached a peace agreement with Aceh separatists in 2005'.

certainty.note: The Revolution's fronts moved with each offensive and the Van Mook line was 'an artificial line which connected the most advanced Dutch tanks' positions'; Republican guerrilla zones behind the Dutch lines are not mapped by the pages.
Judgment: a recognised state with surveyed land and treaty maritime borders; no page opened dates the boundary agreements.
